question.text: This river has its origins in the Blue and White rivers and, thanks to the Aswan Dam, is not flooding as much as it used to.
question.clue: The Bari and related peoples migrated up this river after the end of the baqt ("bukt") treaty, which caused kingdoms led from Soba and Dongola to decline and allowed the Funj Sultanate to expand along this river.

swap.leadin: Two Hittite spies were tortured in the prelude to this battle, and one side in this battle was commanded by Muwatallis II.
swap.text: Name this 1274 BCE battle in which the Ra and Ptah divisions contributed to the largest chariot battle in history.
swap.clue: In this battle, the Ra and Amun divisions were initially routed by attacks across the Orontes River launched by Muwatalli II.

question.leadin: Answer the following about famous archaeological finds in Egypt.
question.text: The 1799 discovery of this large fragment of a black stele [stee-lee] allowed scholars to understand hieroglyphs, since it included Greek, Demotic, and heiroglphyic translations of a law.
question.clue: That rediscovery occurred in 1799 while the French soldier Pierre-Francois Bouchard was on the Napoleonic campaign in Egypt.

swap.text: This young pharaoh, the son of Akhenaten, had his tomb excavated by Howard Carter.
swap.clue: George Herbert financed a mission in the Valley of the Kings that stumbled upon the resting place of this Pharaoh, son of Akhenaten.

question.leadin: The layout of a city built by this ruler was detailed in the Boundary Stelae, which were carved into a tall cliffside.
question.text: Name this ruler. This pharaoh notoriously tried to implement a monotheistic religion centered around a solar deity represented by a golden disk.
question.clue: His wife was the daughter of Ay and he constructed many temples near Karnak to a certain solar god.

swap.leadin: This son of Seti I commissioned a temple for his wife Nefertari.
swap.text: Name this Egyptian ruler known for his construction projects, such as the statues of himself at Abu Simbel.
swap.clue: This man succeeded his father Seti I as pharaoh, and his favorite consort was Nefertari.

question.leadin: Much like Chip Beall, the people of this time period were anti-pyramidal, eschewing ostentatious tombs for ones cut out of rock, which were easier to conceal and protect.
question.text: Name this unsteady time in Egyptian history beginning with unification under Mentuhotep I and ending with Egypt being conquered by the Hyksos; that is, the first and second Intermediate Periods.
question.clue: The fnal rulers of this period were called the Xois Dynasty since they moved the capital there.

swap.text: By the Fourth Dynasty, the Egyptian Pharaoh Khufu had erected this pyramid, the largest of the Egyptian pyramids and the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
swap.answerHtml: Great Pyramid of Giza [or Great Pyramid at Giza; prompt on Giza Pyramid or Pyramid of Cheops]
swap.clue: Slave labor was long thought to have been used to build this structure, but many archaeologists believe that thousands of skilled laborers were used instead over a 20 year period.

question.leadin: This region's Queen Ati was depicted in an ancient relief at the Deir el-Bahri (DAYR el-BAHR-i) complex.
question.text: Name this region from which a 16th-century B.C. Egyptian expedition brought back frankincense and live myrrh trees.
question.clue: An expedition to this place led by the Chancellor Nehsi was recorded in inscriptions in the mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahri.

swap.text: Ramses' tomb was found at this site on the west bank of the Nile. Howard Carter excavated the tomb of King Tut at this site, which contains the remains of several New Kingdom rulers.
swap.clue: The financier behind an excavation at this site died from an infected mosquito bite, which sparked rumors that a location at this site was cursed.

question.text: During Napoleon's Egyptian campaign, his troops apocryphally fired a stray cannonball that knocked the nose off of this monument. This Egyptian monument depicts a mythical creature with a human head and a lion's body.
question.clue: The Dream Stele was constructed next to this object by Thutmose IV ("TOOT-mose the fourth").

swap.leadin: Identify the following about an ancient civilization.
swap.text: The fall of the Hittite Empire in the 12th century BC was brought about by invasions by these groups, who may have been Bronze Age Greeks or Sicilians, but whose name derived from the source of their invasion.
swap.clue: Egypt fought them under Merneptah and Ramses III, and they destroyed the Hittites.

question.leadin: This man's architectural achievements include the enlargement of the Temple of Amon and the construction of Cleopatra's Needles.
question.text: Identify this pharaoh of the 18th dynasty who reigned from 1479 to 1426 B.C.E.
question.clue: This ruler's most famous victory was a seven-month siege of Canaanites.

swap.text: The Armana letters were written during this period of ancient Egyptian history. This period followed the second intermediate period and marked Egypt at the height of its power.
swap.clue: The first ruler of it was known as the "son of the moon-god Iah" and erected the Tempest Stele and Donation Stele.

question.leadin: Herodotus claimed the thickness of Egyptian skulls at this battle was explained by not wearing turbans, and noted that Polycrates of Samos sent forty warships of unreliable scoundrels to take part.
question.text: Name this 525 BC battle in which the Egyptian Psamtik III fell after the Greek general Phanes directed the Persians to some Arabs who helped them cross the Sinai desert.

swap.text: On his return journey, Bombo stops at this city, that was once named Rhakotis. Travel websites recommend that you visit the Mameluke era Qaitbay Fort and explore the Kom al-Shuqafa catacombs in this city.
swap.clue: This city's serapeum was destroyed on the orders of Theophilus.

question.leadin: Identify the following about monumental columns.
question.text: Constructed of red Aswan granite, this Corinthian column, which despite its name was actually constructed by Diocletian to commemorate his defeat of the Alexandrian revolt, stands atop the former ground of the Serapeum.

swap.text: Little is known about him except for his Great Pyramid and the five boats buried next to it.
swap.clue: This pharaoh whose reign saw the construction of the first and largest pyramid at Giza.

question.leadin: This historian's work partially survives through quotations in Josephus's polemic Against Apion.
question.text: Name this Egyptian priest, who was commissioned to write a history of Egypt called the Aegyptiaca during the Ptolemaic period. This historian divided the history of Egypt into thirty dynasties of mortal kings.
question.clue: Continuations of this priest's historical work have been written by the Libyan Apion and Chaeremon.

swap.leadin: According to Polybius' Histories, a man named Theodotus the Aetolian tried to assassinate Ptolemy IV the night before this battle, but he snuck into the wrong tent and killed his physician.
swap.text: Name this 219 BC battle between Egypt and the Seleucid Empire.
swap.clue: This battle in which Ptolemy IV repelled a Seleucid invasion in 217 BCE.
